title: EGS interperiod linkage: thermal decline and myopic vintage handling
body: ## Changes proposed in this Pull Request This PR fixes two related bugs affecting EGS generators in multi-period (both myopic and perfect foresight) runs, and adds myopic-specific logic to correctly enforce generator vintage years. --- 1. EGS thermal decline (capacity factor profiles) EGS generators were running at a flat p_max_pu = 1.0 in all periods instead of exhibiting the thermal drawdown encoded in the Aljubran et al. (2024) FGEM supply curves. Two bugs in attach_egs (add_electricity.py) caused this: Bug A — sub_id dtype mismatch (the blocking bug): bus2sub.csv stores sub_ids as float strings ("39763.0") while profile_EGS.nc stores them as integer strings ("39763"). The pd.merge on sub_id found zero matches, so no EGS generators were added to the base network at all. EGS then fell through to attach_multihorizon_new_generators in add_extra_components, which created spatially uniform generators with p_max_pu = 1 and no resource constraints. Fixed by normalizing bus2sub["sub_id"] to integer strings before the merge. Bug B — MultiIndex year level type mismatch: After the merge fix, the bus_profiles pivot table has a MultiIndex with a float64 outer level (2030.0, 2040.0, 2050.0) while n.snapshots uses int32 periods (2030, 2040, 2050). PyPSA silently filled the mismatched entries with the default p_max_pu = 1.0. Fixed by casting the outer level to int and reindexing bus_profiles to n.snapshots before passing it to n.madd. With both fixes, the FGEM-derived thermal drawdown is now correctly applied: years 1–10 of production (~CF 0.86), years 11–20 (~CF 0.81), and the steep decline in years 21–30 (~CF 0.28) are reflected across investment periods. Each new investment vintage correctly starts at year-1 production via the shift logic in attach_multihorizon_egs. add_extra_components.py: Also removes the original (build_year=0) EGS generators after vintaged copies are created for each investment period. Without this, the originals remain active across all periods, accumulate capacity through prepare_brownfield, and compound the geological resource across periods. --- 2. Myopic mode: generator vintage and resource constraints In myopic mode (multi_investment_periods=False), PyPSA solves each investment period independently without natively enforcing build_year. This allows future-vintage generators to be built or dispatched before their intended period, and allows the full EGS supply-curve resource to be re-invested in each period. Three functions added to solve_network.py: - mask_future_generators — Before each period solve, zeros out p_nom, p_nom_max, and p_nom_extendable for any generator with build_year > planning_horizon, preventing the optimizer from using capacity that hasn't been unlocked yet. State is saved for restoration after the solve. - restore_future_generators — Restores the masked generator parameters after the solve so they are available in subsequent periods. - update_egs_p_nom_max — Caps EGS p_nom_max for the current period by subtracting capacity already built (locked-in) in prior periods at the same bus. This enforces the shared geological resource constraint that perfect foresight handles natively but myopic mode would otherwise ignore, allowing the full resource to be re-built in every period. --- Files changed: scripts/add_electricity.py, scripts/add_extra_components.py, scripts/solve_network.py, scripts/plot_statistics.py --- ## Checklist - [x] I tested my contribution locally and it seems to work fine. - [x] Code and workflow changes are sufficiently documented. - [ ] Changed dependencies are added to `envs/environment.yaml`. - [ ] Changes in configuration options are added in all of `config.default.yaml`. - [ ] Changes in configuration options are also documented in `doc/configtables/*.csv`.

title: Calibrate TAMU transmission capacity using REEDS data
body:
Closes #686.

## Changes proposed in this Pull Request
1. Simplify and cluster tamu grid to county/reeds zone/state-level as normal
2. For the lines that exist in both tamu and reeds, calibrate the line capacity of the clustered tamu grid by `np.maximum(reeds_data['mw_f0'], reeds_data['mw_r0']) / s_max_pu`, and adjust line parameters proportionally.
3. For the lines that exist in tamu but not in reeds, delete them from the network.
4. For the lines that exist in reeds but not in tamu, add them into the network. Use the average per-unit r, x, b, g to estimate their line parameters.
